beat: The fringe corpus - tracing underground-facility claims backwards to their earliest traceable appearance (Denver International Airport, Dulce, DUMBs, the Phil Schneider material, claimed tunnel networks, and the older strata beneath them)
method_notes:
WHAT I ACTUALLY DID, AND THE ONE FACT THAT GOVERNS EVERYTHING BELOW.

I resolved nothing. Not one citation in this file was retrieved to bytes. WebSearch works in this container; WebFetch is blocked for essentially every host that matters. I attempted four fetches and all four returned EGRESS_BLOCKED: archives.denverlibrary.org (the New World Airport Commission finding aid), www.loc.gov (the HAER survey for Wright-Patterson Building 18), digital.library.unt.edu (the mirror of LA-5354-MS), and cdnc.ucr.edu (the San Pedro News Pilot page of 30 January 1934). Those four are, not coincidentally, the four most diagnostic items I found. Everything else in this file is a search-result title or summary. Under BES 2.2 every row here is receipt_state UNRESOLVED-UNREACHABLE, receipt_class R-NONE, membership V0 - arithmetically inert on every condition, retained and displayed. V is empty for every proposition in this file, which means CAP-5 caps every one of them at F, and SCI is approximately 0, which under 9.4 step 2 returns X instead. That is why nearly every proposed_band reads 'X - VERIFICATION PENDING' with a named ceiling. It is the correct answer, not a hedge.

The distinction I have tried to hold on every line: a search summary describing a document is evidence that a description exists. It is not evidence of the document's contents. Where I state a report number, a patent number, an archival identifier or a date, it came from a search-result title or snippet and NOT from my own recall - and I have said so at each one. I generated no identifiers. Where I had no URL I left the field empty and marked the source CITED-BY-OTHERS-NOT-SEEN rather than constructing a plausible address. The one place I constructed a URL is the Google Patents address for US 3,693,731, and I have flagged it in the source record as constructed rather than retrieved.

WHAT I SEARCHED. Roughly twenty targeted queries, built backwards from claims to artifacts rather than forwards from claims to descriptions: origin-artifact queries pinning a person, a date and a venue (Shufelt/LA Times January 1934; Dorr's notarised affidavit; the Coast to Coast broadcast of 21 February 1997; Lewin's NYTBR recantation; Amazing Stories March 1945; the Preparedness Expo lecture; Pollock 1976; the Goldwater letter of 28 March 1975; Chardy's Miami Herald piece of 5 July 1987); mundane-alternative queries designed to find the specific thing a claim is mistaking itself for (Wright-Patterson Building 18's real identity; the New World Airport Commission's real charter; the real DIA baggage tunnels; the Rainier Mesa U12 complex; Kittitas County property records); and documentary-kernel queries testing whether a fringe claim sits on a real record (the nuclear subterrene report series and patent; the Iran-Contra hearing exchange).

WHAT WORKED. Backward origin-tracing works remarkably well against an indexed web, because origins are dated artifacts and dated artifacts are indexable. Mundane-alternative hunting worked better than I expected and produced the two best findings in the file - the Denver Public Library's processed archival collection for the New World Airport Commission, and the Library of Congress HAER survey identifying Wright-Patterson Building 18 as a Power Plant Laboratory Complex. Both are affirmative undercutting rows at instance scope from bodies with authority over the fact, which is a different and much stronger thing than an absence, and both are unreachable from here.

WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH, STATED PLAINLY. (1) Not one ORIGIN grade in this file is earned, because an ORIGIN proposition under BES requires a dated earliest artifact WITH a logged negative receipt across the canonical ORIGIN corpora - Wayback CDX with collapse=digest, IA full-text hits_inside, the AFU newsletter runs, UTZOO, Arctic Shift, Chronicling America and Open ONI - showing no earlier appearance. I ran zero of those. I can say where a claim is FOUND. I cannot yet say where it ORIGINATES, and the difference is the whole proposition class. (2) I could not test whether the convergent origin chains I kept finding are independent reconstructions or one account propagated; under BES 5.1.7's default they are SAME lineage and I have treated them so. (3) I could not verify a single one of the record numbers I am passing along.

ONE THING I WANT ON THE RECORD ABOUT MY OWN OUTPUT. I am one model running one set of weights. Under BES 5.0 and 5.1.2 everything in this file is ONE lineage, capped at one by construction, and if another agent in this fleet returns the same claims that is not corroboration - it is the same witness speaking twice. My fan-out exists for recall. It contributes nothing to confirmation and I have not written a line as though it does.

candidates.name: Dulce Base, Archuleta Mesa, Rio Arriba County, New Mexico
candidates.era: Claim originates 1979-1980; expands 1987-1991; aggregated and vastly extended through the 1990s
candidates.jurisdiction: Rio Arriba County, New Mexico; Jicarilla Apache Nation lands adjoin the claimed location

location.description: Archuleta Mesa, north of the village of Dulce, New Mexico, on or adjacent to Jicarilla Apache Nation land near the Colorado state line. I hold no receipted coordinate. The claim itself has never been given consistent coordinates by its own sources.
location.basis: Place name only, from search summaries. No parcel, no PLSS description, no coordinate was retrieved. I have not invented one.

propositions.statement: The Dulce underground-base claim first appears with Paul Bennewitz in Albuquerque, 1979-1980, and acquires its canonical multi-level-facility form through Thomas Allen LeVesque writing as 'Jason Bishop III' (1989) and the 'Thomas Castello' persona (c. 1987-1991), then through Bruce Alan Walton writing as 'BRANTON'.
propositions.assessment: This is the proposition where the record is strongest and where the register can say something affirmative. Search summaries consistently give the same chain with the same dates, and the chain is not merely asserted: LeVesque is a real, dated, findable person (1948-2018) with a Wikipedia biography; his 1989 authorship of 'The Dulce Base' under the Bishop pseudonym is attributed in multiple summaries; and Norio Hayakawa published a dated post (2016) identifying LeVesque as the personality behind the Dulce story, followed by a 2021 post reporting LeVesque's admission that Castello never existed. What I have NOT done is the thing an ORIGIN grade actually requires under BES: the dated earliest artifact retrieved with a receipt, PLUS a logged negative receipt across the canonical ORIGIN corpora (Wayback CDX, IA hits_inside, the AFU newsletter runs, UTZOO, Arctic Shift) establishing that no earlier appearance exists. I ran none of those. I have search summaries describing a lineage, which is evidence that a description of a lineage exists.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING (SCI approximately 0; V empty; ceiling if the 1989 Bishop text and the pre-1985 newsletter run resolve with a negative receipt behind them: A). The register's own calibration case A-12 already fixes this at A; nothing I found moves it, and nothing I found independently establishes it.
supporting: Wikipedia, 'Thomas Allen LeVesque' - a standing biographical article dating him 1948-2018 and naming the Jason Bishop III pseudonym and the 1989 'The Dulce Base' text (search snippet only)
Norio Hayakawa, 'The mysterious Jason Bishop III...', noriohayakawa.wordpress.com, dated 27 November 2016 (search snippet only)
Norio Hayakawa, 'Thomas E. Castello never existed, admitted the late Tal Levesque...', dated 23 April 2021 (search snippet only)
Greg Bishop, 'Project Beta' (Paraview Pocket Books / Simon & Schuster, 2005) - the reconstruction of the Bennewitz affair (search snippet only; ISBN 9780743470926 appears in bookseller listings)
undercutting: None found against the origin chain itself. That is unsurprising and uninformative: I did not search the corpora in which an earlier appearance would live.

A structural caution that cuts against my own confidence: every summary I read gives the SAME chain in the SAME order. Under BES 5.1.6 that is a signature of one account propagated, not of independent reconstruction. The chain may all descend from Greg Bishop 2005 plus Hayakawa. I could not test that.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: For an ORIGIN proposition, a dated artifact IS the evidence, so a resolved 1989 text would be D4 on its face. But the diagnosticity here is entirely in the negative receipt, not the positive one: showing the claim exists in 1989 is trivial, showing nothing earlier exists is the whole assertion, and I have not run a single one of the searches that would establish it. My positive evidence therefore discriminates nothing at all between 'the claim began in 1979-89' and 'the claim began earlier and these are the copies that survived indexing'.

propositions.statement: A substantial artificial subsurface structure exists beneath or within Archuleta Mesa, New Mexico.
propositions.assessment: Nothing I retrieved supports this and one thing I retrieved cuts against it. The strongest single item is that Gabe Valdez - a New Mexico State Police officer, resolvable in unrelated records because his cattle-mutilation investigations were reported in the contemporaneous press from 1976, and placed in exactly the role asserted - concluded before his death in 2011 that the mutilations were environmental-contamination sampling connected to 1960s nuclear testing and that the objects reported around Archuleta Mesa were government aircraft. That is a named, position-to-know, in-role denial from the investigating officer, which BES 5.4 scores normally as UNDERCUTS. It is reported to me by search summaries of a Santa Fe New Mexican article and of a book by his son Greg Valdez, so it is second-hand and unreceipted.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING (SCI approximately 0). Ceiling if the Valdez material and the county/BLM/Jicarilla land records resolve: R. The register's calibration case R-05 already fixes this at R (R1), on LeVesque's admission. I flag one honest weakness in that route below.
supporting: None. I found no record of any class supporting a structure.
undercutting: Santa Fe New Mexican article summary reporting Gabe Valdez's own conclusion that the mutilations were environmental sampling tied to 1960s nuclear testing on Jicarilla Apache land and that the Archuleta Mesa objects were government aircraft (search snippet only)
LeVesque's reported admission to Adam Gorightly that the Dulce material, including Castello, was fabricated creative writing (search snippet only, via Hayakawa 2021)
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Valdez's denial discriminates strongly, because the mundane alternative does not require a named investigating officer to affirmatively state that the anomalies had a different cause; it merely permits it. The LeVesque admission is the R1 trigger the register relies on. But note what R1 requires: 'an admission by a participant'. What exists is a THIRD-PARTY REPORT of an admission by a participant, relayed by Gorightly and republished by Hayakawa, after LeVesque's death. Under BES 5.4 attestation custody, an account of what a named person said is one lineage with whoever is asserting it, not with the person. That does not make it false - Gorightly and Hayakawa are both named, dated and findable - but it means the R1 route rests on unreceipted second-hand testimony about a dead man, and the register should say so rather than treat R1 as clean.

propositions.statement: A joint human and non-human research and detention facility of seven or more sublevels operated at Dulce.
propositions.assessment: V is empty for this proposition and the artifacts that carry it are authored by the claimants, whose probative content is the claim itself - the BES 2.5 self-attestation exclusion in its cleanest form. Nothing survives to be graded. This is F-shaped, not R-shaped: nothing affirmatively contradicts a seven-level facility because there is nothing there to contradict.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING on search completeness; provisional band F (CAP-5, V empty) once the canonical EXIST/FUNCTION search set is executed with logged negative receipts.
undercutting: Same Valdez material as above, which speaks to the anomalies rather than to the sublevels
propositions.diagnosticity_note: No observation I hold discriminates. The sublevel-numbering convention itself is the diagnostic feature worth recording: BES-relevant because when it appears attached to a DIFFERENT real facility, it is evidence of textual descent from this cluster rather than of independent observation.

propositions.statement: A US Air Force Office of Special Investigations disinformation operation was conducted against Paul Bennewitz in the early 1980s.
propositions.assessment: This is the real documentary kernel under the folklore and it deserves separate grading, because it is the part most likely to be true and it is the part the fringe corpus got closest to. Richard Doty, an AFOSI special agent, has stated on the record in multiple named venues that he fed Bennewitz false material and produced hoaxed documents. Doty's AFOSI employment is the sort of fact that should be resolvable in records created for unrelated purposes, which would satisfy the position-to-know clause. But the CONTENT of the operation is Doty's own attestation about his own conduct, decades later, by a person whose credibility is itself contested - and self-serving admission is still self-attestation about an unwitnessed act. Greg Bishop's 2005 book is the disciplined secondary reconstruction.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING. Ceiling if AFOSI personnel or investigative records resolve: B or better. On Doty's testimony alone the honest ceiling is C, and lower if his position-to-know record does not resolve.
supporting: The Debrief, 'Richard Doty: Disinformation, Paul Bennewitz, and UAP Whistleblower Fallout' (search snippet only)
HuffPost, 'Ex-Air Force Law Enforcement Agent Says He Hoaxed Major UFO Mythologies' (search snippet only)
KLAS/8newsnow Mystery Wire interview with Doty (search snippet only)
Greg Bishop, 'Project Beta', 2005 (search snippet only)
undercutting: Doty's account of his own activities has been disputed within the same community that reports it; I did not retrieve the specific disputes and cannot weigh them.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A documented AFOSI disinformation operation discriminates powerfully IF established, because it supplies a complete alternative generator for the entire Dulce corpus - and it is the one alternative that explains why the material has the texture of official documents. It also carries a trap: an operation that produced hoaxed documents means that ANY apparently-official document surfacing from this lineage is presumptively suspect, which raises rather than lowers the verification bar on everything downstream.

candidates.mundane_alternative: A11, claim fabricated - specifically, a fabrication generated inside a documented AFOSI disinformation operation against one man, then extended as deliberate creative writing by LeVesque. The co-null is A12, a decommissioned facility of a different known typology: Project Gasbuggy, the 1967 Plowshare nuclear detonation, is roughly 21 miles from Dulce and is a real, documented, government-caused subsurface anomaly in the same district. Distinguishing them: Gasbuggy is at INSTANCE scope for Gasbuggy and ADJACENT for Archuleta Mesa, so under BES 2.4 it is excluded from V here entirely - proximity is not support, and it is equally not a substitute. What would actually distinguish: BLM/Jicarilla land-status records, a spoil-volume signature for an excavation of the claimed scale, or any procurement trace. None retrieved.
candidates.claim_origin: Paul Bennewitz, Albuquerque, 1979-1980, generating the raw material while being fed disinformation; Myrna Hansen's 1980 hypnotic regression supplying the underground imagery; Thomas Allen LeVesque as 'Jason Bishop III' authoring 'The Dulce Base' in 1989; the 'Thomas Castello' persona circulated c. 1987-1991; Bruce Alan Walton as 'BRANTON' aggregating and expanding through the 1990s. LeVesque reportedly admitted before his 2018 death that Castello never existed. I traced this through search summaries only; I did not retrieve the 1989 text, and I ran none of the negative searches that an ORIGIN grade requires.
candidates.expected_records: For a facility of the claimed scale on or adjacent to tribal and federal land: BLM land-status and MLRS records (X2), a Jicarilla Apache Nation land record (X2), a spoil-volume signature for an excavation of the asserted magnitude (X3 - the universal floor for excavation of this size, and the most damaging absence available here), a procurement trace above 50M USD for an appropriated agency (X3), county deed records for any private parcel touched (X3). None of these absences is surprising for a classified facility; ALL of them are surprising for a facility of the asserted physical scale, because spoil and money are not classifiable. That is the correct reading and it is why this is not a case where silence protects the claim.
candidates.lineage_note: Every summary I read gives the identical chain in the identical order with the identical dates. Under BES 5.1.6 that is consistent with one reconstruction propagated, most plausibly Greg Bishop 2005 plus Hayakawa, rather than with independent corroboration. I treat the whole set as ONE lineage under the default-SAME rule and record that I could not test it.
candidates.confidence_note: The origin trace is the register's strongest available product here, and it is also the part I could least verify. I resolved nothing. The one genuinely new thing I can offer is a caution rather than a finding: the R1 refutation route depends on a second-hand report of a dead man's admission, and the register should carry that caveat explicitly rather than present R1 as settled.

candidates.name: Denver International Airport - claimed hardened federal facility beneath the terminal
aliases: the deep underground base at DIA
candidates.era: Airport opened 28 February 1995; the underground-facility claim enters circulation 1993-1996
candidates.jurisdiction: City and County of Denver, Colorado (the airport parcel lies in Denver, surrounded by Adams County)

location.description: Beneath the Jeppesen Terminal and concourses, Denver International Airport, Denver, Colorado.
location.basis: Named airport and municipality only, from search summaries. No receipted coordinate, no parcel identifier, no plan sheet. None invented.

propositions.statement: The specific claim of a multi-level hardened complex beneath DIA - 'eight levels', a '4.5 square mile underground city', an '88.5 square mile base' - originates with Phil Schneider and was propagated in print by Alex Christopher, whose 'Pandora's Box' appeared in 1993 and whose 'Pandora's Box II: The Denver International Airport Story' followed in 1996.
propositions.assessment: This is the most useful thing I found on this beat, and it is a LINEAGE finding rather than a new site. Search summaries of Christopher's own text attribute the specific figures to Schneider directly. If that holds, then the DIA claim and the '129 DUMBs' claim are not two independent bodies of folklore that happen to agree - they share a terminus in one man's 1995 lecture circuit. Under BES 5.7 that is the non-monotone case: discovering the link MERGES two lineages and can lower a grade rather than raise it. The register should record it as such. I have not read Christopher's text; I have search summaries of a scanned copy on Internet Archive and of at least two mirror transcriptions.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING (SCI approximately 0). Ceiling if the 1993 and 1996 texts resolve with dated custody and the Wayback/Usenet negative receipt is run: A. Note that the ORIGIN grade for DIA is not in the calibration set; only the FUNCTION grade (E-01) is.
supporting: archive.org item 'pandoras-box-ii-the-denver-international-airport-story-by-alex-christopher' - a dated, addressable IA identifier (search snippet only; I did not open it)
Two mirror transcriptions of the same text (docshare.tips, pdfcoffee.com) - copies, not independent sources
A dated KSEO interview transcript with Alex Christopher, 26 April 1996 (search snippet only)
undercutting: None found. I did not run the Wayback CDX or Usenet checks that would test whether the claim predates 1993.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: For ORIGIN, a dated artifact is the evidence. The distinctive numerals - 8 levels, 4.5 square miles, 88.5 square miles - function as a fingerprint in exactly the way BES 5.1.7's distinctive-error test describes: they are idiosyncratic, unsourced, and carried forward verbatim, so any page bearing them is in this lineage. That is a genuinely discriminating test and it survives paraphrase.

propositions.statement: Large underground works exist at Denver International Airport.
propositions.assessment: True, boring, and documented - and it is the reason this entry cannot be dismissed as pure fabrication. The airport's own operators acknowledge multiple subterranean levels beneath the main terminal: the passenger train tunnels between concourses, and the abandoned BAE automated baggage system with its 26 miles of steel track and 35-plus miles of conveyor, walled off after the system was retired in 2008. Reporting in 2025-2026 indicates the airport intends to convert some of those disused baggage tunnels into pedestrian walkways with construction from 2027. That last detail is the most evidentially interesting thing on this entry: an operator opening the voids to the public is a strong future UNDERCUTS row against the concealed-facility reading.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING on my own search; substantively this is the register's A-grade half. Calibration E-01 already carries EXIST(large underground works at DIA) at A on T1 records. I resolved none of them.
supporting: 9News investigation into the underground tunnels of DIA (search snippet only)
Fox News report that the airport will open tunnels to the public (search snippet only)
Visit Denver and multiple trade summaries describing the BAE system's 26 miles of track and its 2008 abandonment (search snippets only; these are secondary and partly promotional)
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Every one of these observations is on the BES universal-D0 list or its equivalent: large excavation volume, tunnels, dedicated electrical load, deep wells, a fuel farm. They are exactly what a very large airport built badly in the early 1990s produces. They establish EXIST and discriminate nothing about function. This is the point of calibration case E-01 and my search reproduced it exactly - six or seven real signals, none diagnostic.

propositions.statement: A hardened non-airport federal facility operates beneath the DIA terminal.
propositions.assessment: V-claim is empty. Everything real I found is a property of the place, not of the claim, and the origin artifacts are self-attesting under BES 2.5 and route to ORIGIN rather than into V. CAP-2b holds the ceiling at E. I add one item the calibration does not carry: the 'New World Airport Commission', whose name is the single most-cited textual hook for the New World Order reading, is a documented real organisation - the Denver Public Library holds a processed archival collection of its records, described as covering public relations for the airport's opening, active 1994, 1997 and 1998, with correspondence to and from its president Charles Ansbacher. A finding aid at the holding repository is a T1 artifact whose issuing body has authority over the fact of what it holds. That is an affirmative, instance-scope UNDERCUTS row against the NWO reading of the name, not merely an absence.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING on my own search; substantively E, per calibration E-01, via CAP-2b. The DPL finding aid, if it resolves, does not move FUNCTION to R - it undercuts one textual hook, not the whole claim - but it belongs in U and should be published.
undercutting: Denver Public Library ArchivesSpace, 'New World Airport Commission Records', repositories/3/resources/6538 (FETCH-BLOCKED by the egress proxy; I have only the search summary of the finding aid)
Westword's reported explanation that the name alludes to Dvorak's New World Symphony (search snippet only, reported at second hand)
The operator's stated intention to open the disused baggage tunnels to the public from 2027 - a future ticketed-access-class negative in BES 4.4 terms
propositions.diagnosticity_note: The DPL finding aid discriminates: a temporary municipal PR commission with a processed archival collection, a named president and a 1994-1998 activity window is not what the New World Order reading predicts, and the mundane reading predicts it exactly. That is an E0-under-H / A3-under-null cell, which the BES 4.4 matrix scores as UNDERCUTS at minus D3. It is the single strongest discriminating item I found anywhere on this beat, and I could not open it.

candidates.mundane_alternative: A07/A08 in combination - a very large civil airport, built over budget in the early 1990s, whose automated baggage system failed catastrophically and left walled-off concrete voids. What would distinguish a concealed hardened facility from that: a structural floor-loading filing, a blast-door or blast-valve line item in a Denver building-department record, a NEPA document specifying CBR filtration or shielding, or a real-property record showing a federal custodial entity for space beneath the terminal. None retrieved, and per BES 6.1 their absence here is genuinely informative rather than routine, because a municipal airport is not a classified-construction authority and its permit record is not structurally withheld.
candidates.claim_origin: Phil Schneider, on the 1994-1995 lecture circuit, supplying the specific figures; Alex Christopher, 'Pandora's Box' (1993) and 'Pandora's Box II: The Denver International Airport Story' (1996), putting them into circulating print and attributing them to Schneider. The 'New World Airport Commission' hook is a real name lifted from a real temporary PR body. I traced this through search summaries; I opened none of the texts.
candidates.expected_records: Denver building-department filings for the terminal (X2 - a municipal permit record is not structurally withheld, so absence of any hardening specification is informative); FPDS/USAspending awards naming federal construction at the site post-2008 (X1 - descriptions are sanitised and place-of-performance is often the contracting office); FRPP entry for a federal asset at a municipal airport (X2); NEPA documentation for the airport as a major federal action (X2). For a MUNICIPAL facility these profiles are meaningfully non-zero, which is what separates DIA from Greenbrier-1991: silence here is not free.
candidates.lineage_note: The DIA claim and the 129-DUMBs claim share a terminus in Schneider. If that holds, they are ONE lineage, not two, and any register treating them as mutually corroborating is double-counting a single 1995 lecture. This is the merge that BES 5.7 says can lower a grade because a link was found.
candidates.confidence_note: The register's calibration already fixes this entry. My contribution is two specific, checkable items: the Schneider-to-Christopher lineage merge, and the Denver Public Library finding aid for the New World Airport Commission as an affirmative undercutting row. Both are search-snippet-only; the DPL host is egress-blocked from this container.

propositions.statement: A US government research programme to develop a nuclear-powered rock-melting tunnelling machine (the 'subterrene') was proposed, funded and prosecuted at Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory in the early 1970s, and was cancelled without a full-scale prototype.
propositions.assessment: This is the strongest 'the fringe was sitting on real documents' case I found, and it is why the beat brief's warning against assuming falsity matters. propositions.statement: The claim originates in a notarised affidavit by Earl Dorr, executed in Pasadena on 16 November 1934, first published in the California Mining Journal, November 1940.
propositions.assessment: Unusually well-specified for a fringe origin, and unusually testable. Search summaries give a notarisation date and place, a publication date and venue six years later, and - importantly - report that at least two versions of the affidavit circulate, one bearing a 10 December 1934 notarisation and claimed by its holder to be the original. Competing versions of a foundational document are a textual-criticism problem, not a rumour problem, and they are resolvable: a notarised instrument leaves a notary journal entry, and the California Mining Journal is a physical serial. The most diagnostic detail I found is negative and cuts against the whole downstream tradition: the affidavit reportedly does not mention Kokoweef Peak, Crystal Cave, or the Peysert brothers at all. If that holds, then the specific location and the Native American provenance story are LATER accretions attached to Dorr's text, not content of it - which is the classic backsourcing result.

candidates.era: Claim originates 21 February 1997; repeated 24 February 1997, 2000 and 2002

location.description: Claimed as rural private property roughly nine miles west of Ellensburg, Kittitas County, Washington, in the Manastash Ridge area. No parcel has ever been identified and organised ground searches have not located any such feature.
location.basis: A claimed distance and direction from a named town, given on air by a person whose existence in the county record has not been established. I hold no coordinate, no parcel and no receipted record, and I have not invented any.

propositions.statement: The claim first appears on the Coast to Coast AM broadcast of 21 February 1997, from a caller identifying himself as Mel Waters, with a second appearance on 24 February 1997 and further appearances in 2000 and 2002.
propositions.assessment: A precisely datable broadcast origin, which is the best kind for this register: the artifact is a dated recording with an addressable identifier convention in the Internet Archive Coast to Coast collections. A dated broadcast is excellent evidence of when a claim entered circulation and no evidence at all of whether it is true - the register should be able to hold both, and here it can. I did not retrieve the recording or confirm the date against the archive's own metadata; I have consistent search summaries.

propositions.diagnosticity_note: A dated broadcast fixes the entry point precisely. It discriminates 'this began in 1997 on national radio' from 'this is an older local tradition that reached radio in 1997' only if the negative search is run - and the DNR geologist's remark about a real local mine shaft (below) is a specific reason to suspect an older local substrate that the broadcast overwrote.

propositions.assessment: The refutation here is unusually strong for a fringe claim and it is affirmative rather than merely absent. Reporters are described as having pulled the Kittitas County records and found no Mel Waters as a property owner, no wife employed at Central Washington University, and no rural parcel matching the description. A county assessor's record is a T1 artifact from a body with authority over the fact of ownership, and a search of it returning no such owner and no such parcel is content, not silence. Separately, an organised ground search of about thirty people with GPS and metal detectors crossed Manastash Ridge in 2002 with a Seattle Times reporter present and found nothing. Under BES 8, that combination is R3-shaped - but only if the county record itself resolves; what I hold is journalists' reports of having searched it.

The county-record negative is diagnostic because a named private landowner in a CONUS county is the single most reliably recorded fact in this whole domain - BES puts county deed and assessor records at X3, the universal floor, and this is precisely the case the floor exists for. Powell's statement is diagnostic on two counts: he is a resolvable named person in exactly the role asserted, employed by the state geological authority, speaking about his own jurisdiction, and he supplies a specific mundane referent rather than a general denial. The 2002 ground search is weaker than it looks - failure to find a feature in mountainous terrain is a genuine but limited negative.

Washington has substantial lidar coverage and this is a genuinely runnable test.

candidates.confidence_note: A strong candidate for the register's clearest published R, if the county record resolves. It is also a useful control: the reason this claim is refutable and Dulce is not is that it names a private parcel in a CONUS county, and that is the most reliably recorded object in American life.

candidates.name: 'Report from Iron Mountain' and the Iron Mountain facility near Hudson, New York
aliases: Report from Iron Mountain on the Possibility and Desirability of Peace
candidates.era: Book published 1967; authorship admitted 19 March 1972; recirculated as genuine from the early 1990s
candidates.jurisdiction: Columbia County, New York (the facility named in the text); the document itself is non-located

location.description: The text names an underground facility 'near the town of Hudson', New York, described as a nuclear hideout used by large American corporations for records storage and substitute headquarters. That describes a real class of facility and, on its face, a real one. I did not establish which specific site.
location.basis: A place name given inside a document I have not read, reported in search summaries. No coordinate, no parcel, none invented.

propositions.statement: The 'Report from Iron Mountain' was written by Leonard C. Lewin, published by Dial Press in 1967, and admitted by Lewin to be a satirical fabrication in the New York Times Book Review of 19 March 1972.
propositions.assessment: One of the very few claims in this entire corpus where the origin is not merely traced but CONFESSED, in a named national publication, by the named author, at a checkable date. Search summaries are consistent: Lewin wrote the whole thing with help including editors of the satire magazine Monocle, framed it as leaked to him by a participant, and recanted in print in 1972. Both artifacts - the 1967 Dial Press first edition and the 19 March 1972 NYT Book Review piece - are ordinary published objects with catalogue records and no classification issues.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING. Ceiling if the 1967 imprint and the dated 1972 NYTBR page resolve: A. This is the strongest available ORIGIN candidate on my beat because the admission is documentary rather than testimonial.
supporting: Wikipedia, 'Leonard C. Lewin' and 'The Report from Iron Mountain', giving the 19 March 1972 New York Times Book Review admission (search snippets only; T4, crowd-edited)
Foreign Policy, 'Trump's Hoax Promotions Are a Longtime U.S. Habit' (2026), treating the episode as a documented hoax (search snippet only)
Multiple full-text mirrors of the 1967 text on fringe hosts - copies, evidentially worthless except as lineage tracers
undercutting: Search results include at least two currently-live pages arguing the text is genuine, including a machine-generated encyclopedia entry. Under BES these are POST-2022-UNATTRIBUTED or T5 and contribute zero lineages, but their presence is the finding: the 1972 admission demonstrably did not settle the matter in circulation.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: An author's signed public recantation in a named periodical is about as diagnostic as ORIGIN evidence gets, and it satisfies BES 8's R1 branch on its face - not a third-party report of an admission, but the admission itself, in print, under the author's own name. Contrast this directly with the Dulce R1 route, which rests on a second-hand account of a dead man. The register should publish the two side by side, because they look identical in a summary and are completely different in kind.

propositions.statement: An underground records-storage and corporate-relocation facility exists near Hudson, New York.
propositions.assessment: Probably true and entirely mundane, and this is the trap the entry exists to close. Lewin's satire worked precisely because he set it in a real place doing a real thing - underground corporate records storage in a former mine in the Hudson Valley. That real facility class is well documented in the commercial record. Note the entity-resolution hazard: the register already holds Iron Mountain / Boyers, Pennsylvania at band A (calibration A-06), which is a DIFFERENT facility in a different state under a different history. Under BES 11.1 these must not merge; name similarity flags and never merges.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING. Ceiling if Columbia County deed and assessor records and the operator's own corporate filings resolve: A. Materially this is a boring true fact.
supporting: The text's own description, which is a description inside a fabricated document and therefore evidence of nothing except what Lewin wrote
General commercial-record descriptions of underground records storage in the Hudson Valley (search snippets only)
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Nothing here discriminates a hardened continuity facility from commercial underground records storage, and nothing needs to - the mundane reading is the documented one and the operator advertises it. This is the SubTropolis pattern: near-maximum place-signals, zero claim-signals, and the correct answer is a boring A on EXIST with an R on anything more.

propositions.statement: A secret federal Special Study Group met at the Iron Mountain facility from August 1963 to March 1966 and produced the report.
propositions.assessment: Affirmatively refuted by the author's own published admission. This is R1 in its cleanest form: the sole origin lineage is shown fabricated by an admission from the participant, published in a named periodical at a fixed date. Everything downstream - the militia-circulated bootleg editions of the 1990s, the current live pages arguing authenticity - is one lineage with the 1967 book.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING on my own retrieval; substantively R (R1) once the 1972 NYTBR page resolves. Not F: something affirmatively resolves against this, which is exactly the R/F distinction BES Part 8 draws.
undercutting: Lewin's admission of authorship, New York Times Book Review, 19 March 1972 (search snippet only)
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A signed authorial recantation is improbable under the proposition that the document is a genuine government report, and near-certain under the proposition that it is a satire. That is the E0/A3 cell and it is affirmative content rather than an absence, which is what BES 8.4 requires before R can fire.

candidates.mundane_alternative: A11 for the report, A06 for the facility - general underground commercial storage in a former Hudson Valley mine. What would distinguish a genuine federal study group from a satire: any appropriations line, any agency record of the group's convening, any named participant, any archival deposit. None exists, and the author says why.

candidates.name: 'Hangar 18' and the 'Blue Room', Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio
candidates.era: Claim cluster from the 1950s-60s; the most-cited artifact is dated 28 March 1975
candidates.jurisdiction: Greene and Montgomery Counties, Ohio; Wright-Patterson AFB, Area B

location.description: Area B, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, near Dayton, Ohio. The Library of Congress HAER survey documents a Building 18 in Area B at the northeast corner of C and Fifth Streets, identified as the Power Plant Laboratory Complex.
location.basis: A named installation and a street intersection given in a HAER survey title retrieved as a search summary. loc.gov is egress-blocked from this container. No coordinate invented.

propositions.statement: The most-cited documentary artifact behind the claim is a letter of 28 March 1975 from Senator Barry Goldwater to Shlomo Arnon, stating that Goldwater had roughly a decade earlier sought access to the building at Wright-Patterson where Air Force UFO material was held and had been refused, and that the material remained classified.
propositions.assessment: This is the fringe artifact on my beat that most deserves careful treatment rather than dismissal, and it is the one where BES's position-to-know gate does the most interesting work. Goldwater is unambiguously real, resolvable in vast quantities of unrelated record, and was a sitting US Senator and an Air Force Reserve major general - so he passes the identity gate trivially and passes a general position-to-know gate as a legislator. But BES 5.4 requires the record to place the person in THE ROLE ASSERTED. The role asserted here is not 'senator' but 'person with knowledge of what is in that building', and by the letter's own content he was refused access - so the letter is affirmative evidence that Goldwater did NOT know what was in the building. It is a strong artifact for a proposition about Goldwater's request and a weak one for any proposition about the building's contents. The related account of a telephone refusal by General Curtis LeMay is second-hand, attributed via a later author, and does not carry the same status.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING. Ceiling if the letter resolves in a Goldwater papers collection (Arizona State University holds his papers) or in a dated facsimile with custody: A for ORIG. Note carefully: A for ORIG here means 'we know exactly what artifact this story rests on', not 'the story is true'.
supporting: Multiple independent-looking secondary accounts giving the same date (28 March 1975), recipient (Shlomo Arnon) and substance (search snippets only; several are T4/T5 hosts)

A CIA reading-room record titled 'Letter to Honorable Barry M. Goldwater from Vernon A. Walters' surfaced in results - a different letter, but evidence that Goldwater-related correspondence exists in released collections (search snippet only; cia.gov is a .gov host and was not retrievable)
undercutting: Every version I found is a secondary retelling. I located no archival citation to the Goldwater papers and no image of the letter from a custodial repository.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: The letter, if resolved, is highly diagnostic for ORIG and close to null for EXIST or FEAT, because its content is a refusal. That asymmetry is the whole point: a genuine artifact by a genuine, powerful, resolvable person can establish precisely one thing and be routinely cited for a different thing.

propositions.statement: 'Hangar 18' names a specific structure at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.
propositions.assessment: This is where the claim comes apart, and it is a genuinely useful refutation because it is a naming error rather than a factual dispute. The Library of Congress HAER survey records Building 18 in Area B as part of the Power Plant Laboratory Complex - an engine and power-plant research facility whose earliest structures date to the Wright Field era - documented under survey number HAER OH-79-AN with photographic coverage. That is not a hangar. Separately, the Foreign Technology Division, which is the organisation the claim is really reaching for, occupied Building 856, built in the 1970s, becoming FASTC in 1992 and NASIC in 2003. So the folklore's 'Hangar 18' conflates a laboratory building number with a hangar, and attaches to it the function of an organisation housed in a different building entirely.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING. Ceiling if the HAER documentation resolves at the Library of Congress: R for the identity claim, on a T1 record from a survey with authority over the fact of what the building is. This is the single most resolvable refutation on this entry and loc.gov is blocked here.
undercutting: Library of Congress HAER OH-79-AN, 'Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Area B, Building 18, Power Plant Laboratory Complex, Northeast corner of C & Fifth Streets, Dayton, Montgomery County, OH' (FETCH-BLOCKED; title retrieved as a search result)
Accounts placing the Foreign Technology Division in Building 856 from the 1970s, and its successors FASTC and NASIC (search snippets only)
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A HAER survey title states the building's identity and function on its face and the survey's issuing authority - the Historic American Engineering Record, under the National Park Service, working with the installation - has authority over that determination. Under BES 3.4 that is a D4-gate candidate for IDNT and for TYPO, and it discriminates completely: a power-plant laboratory complex is not a hangar and the null does not have to strain at all to produce the documentation.

propositions.statement: Substantial subsurface vaults or complexes exist beneath Wright-Patterson AFB.
propositions.assessment: Genuinely unresolved and I decline to close it. A major inter-war and Second World War aeronautical research installation with power-plant laboratories, wind tunnels and test cells will have real subsurface structures - utility tunnels, test chambers, basements - and the claim that 'underground vaults exist' is close to trivially true for any facility of this class while telling you nothing. The specific assertions I found come from investigators who toured the base and inferred a vast system from what they saw, which is interpretation and takes their tier, not the base's.
propositions.proposed_band: X - NOT ASSESSED. SCI approximately 0; the canonical EXIST set was not run. Any grade here would be manufactured.
supporting: Accounts by Bill Jones and Irena Scott describing a toured facility and inferring extensive subsurface works (search snippets only; interpretation by named non-custodial parties, T5 under BES 3.1 until independently confirmed)
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Basements, tunnels and vaults are on the BES universal-D0 list. For a research installation of this age they are expected under every hypothesis, so they discriminate nothing, and a visitor's impression of extent is an interpretation that inherits the visitor's tier.

propositions.statement: Recovered non-human craft or bodies were or are stored in a facility at Wright-Patterson.
propositions.assessment: V-claim is empty on everything I retrieved. The Goldwater letter records a refusal, not a content. The witness accounts are unresolved. CAP-2b holds the ceiling at E even before anything else is considered.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING on search completeness; provisional E if any verified third-party record of real facts enters V, otherwise F. Note the E/F line: unlike Montauk, there ARE real third-party records here (the base, the FTD, the classification posture), so this may sit at E rather than F once the search set is run.
undercutting: The Goldwater letter's own content - a refusal of access is not knowledge of contents
propositions.diagnosticity_note: No observation I hold discriminates. Expected-record reasoning is nearly useless here in both directions: an Air Force installation's internal storage records are structurally withheld (X0), so silence carries almost no information, and that is the correct and unsatisfying answer.

candidates.mundane_alternative: A08 plus a naming error - an ordinary, very large, genuinely classified military research installation whose real Foreign Technology Division work on recovered FOREIGN (Soviet and Chinese) aircraft is documented, misread as work on non-terrestrial material, with the building number of an unrelated power-plant laboratory attached to it. What would distinguish: any real-property record, CATCODE, or engineering drawing for a storage facility of the claimed type; any AFHRA unit history for the relevant organisation. None retrieved.
candidates.claim_origin: A diffuse mid-century cluster rather than a single text - which is itself a finding, and distinguishes this from Dulce and Montauk. The single most-cited documentary anchor is Goldwater's 28 March 1975 letter to Shlomo Arnon. The 'Hangar 18' name was cemented by a 1980 feature film of that title, which I did not investigate and which the register should trace, because a movie title propagating back into the nomenclature would be a textbook citogenesis event.
candidates.expected_records: AFHRA unit histories by IRIS number for the Foreign Technology Division and predecessors (X1 - the AFHRA index is public but most content is not digitised, flag ARCHIVE-GAP); real-property and CATCODE records for Area B buildings (X1-X2); HAER and NRHP documentation for Area B historic structures (X2-X3 - and these appear to exist); NPRC personnel files for USAF 1947-1964 (X0, RECORD-DESTROYED, the 1973 St. Louis fire). The last is a genuine and underappreciated constraint on every mid-century Wright-Patterson witness claim and the register should carry it explicitly.
candidates.lineage_note: The Goldwater letter appears across many hosts in near-identical wording, which is one lineage. The HAER record and the FTD building history are institutional and independent of the claim by BES 5.1.7's access test.
candidates.confidence_note: I have graded the naming claim harder than the substantive one, deliberately. The identity refutation is resolvable, cheap and decisive; the storage claim is not resolvable from open records and I decline to pretend otherwise. Treating a famous claim fairly sometimes means refusing to close it.

propositions.statement: The figures - approximately 129 or 131 active secret underground bases in the United States, approximately 1,477 worldwide, at 17 to 19 billion dollars each - originate in Phil Schneider's 1995 Preparedness Expo lecture and have no antecedent.
propositions.assessment: The artifact is solid and unusually convenient: a dated recording deposited on the Internet Archive under the identifier 'philexpo'. A dated recording is excellent evidence of when a claim entered circulation. The register's own source registry already flags that the pre-1995 negative check has NOT been run and should be - and I did not run it either. So the honest statement is that I have an artifact and no negative receipt, which means I can say where the claim is FOUND and not yet that it ORIGINATES there. That distinction is the entire content of the ORIGIN proposition class and I am not entitled to skip it.

What I did find is a new and specific citogenesis observation that I have not seen recorded, and it is worth the entry on its own. The phrase 'Western Virginia Office of Controlled Conflict Operations' - which appears to be a Pollock-era coinage carrying no documentary attestation I could find - now appears as an ALTERNATE OFFICIAL NAME in the page titles of both the FAS Nuclear Information Project and GlobalSecurity: 'Mount Weather / High Point Special Facility (SF) / Western Virginia Office of Controlled Conflict Operations'. FAS is a T2/T3 source in this register's own tier table and GlobalSecurity is T4. A folklore coinage that has migrated into the nomenclature of two reference sites that researchers treat as institutional is exactly the laundering pattern CAP-3 exists to catch, and it is happening in the register's own source list.

propositions.statement: A federal emergency-planning exercise designated REX 84 existed in 1984, and contingency planning involving continuity of government, population movement and detention of aliens was the subject of public congressional attention in July 1987.
propositions.assessment: This is a real documentary kernel and the register should say so plainly. Alfonso Chardy, an investigative reporter for the Miami Herald, published on 5 July 1987 an account of Reagan-era emergency contingency planning; Chardy is a real, named, Pulitzer-associated journalist and the article is an ordinary published artifact. More importantly the matter reached the congressional record: on 13 July 1987 Representative Jack Brooks questioned Oliver North about contingency provisions during the Iran-Contra hearings, and that exchange, if it occurred as described, is in a published hearing transcript - a T1 record from a body with authority over its own proceedings. That is a genuinely resolvable D4-gate candidate sitting under a claim that is usually dismissed wholesale. The register's own source registry flags this cluster as 'COG-folklore fingerprints with real documentary kernels underneath' and I think that is exactly right.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING. Ceiling if the Iran-Contra hearing transcript resolves at GovInfo or in the published committee volumes and the Chardy article resolves: A for a carefully worded PROGRAM proposition. Note the wording matters enormously: 'contingency planning existed and was publicly questioned' is A-capable; 'a plan to suspend the Constitution was adopted' is not the same proposition and is not supported by anything I retrieved.

That gap is this entry's whole point. It also carries the BES 1.4 lesson: PROGRAM is clamp-exempt, so a well-documented planning programme can sit at a high band beside an EXIST at F without contradiction - the DUCC pattern again.

propositions.assessment: Nothing supports this. The underground element does not appear in the 1987 disclosure at all as far as I can tell; it is a later accretion, and the circulating site lists resolve either to nothing or to existing publicly-known installations. The related 'H.R. 645' item is a real bill - a National Emergency Centers Establishment Act introduced in 2009 - which was introduced and not enacted, and which concerns above-ground centres on existing military installations. A real bill that was introduced and died is a documented PROGRAM fact and a refutation of the constructed-facility claim in the same object.

propositions.statement: The template for an American 'vast inhabited underground facility' narrative - a multi-level cavern world, a hidden population, advanced technology, and a claimant reporting personal experience presented as fact inside a fiction venue - is fixed by Richard Sharpe Shaver's 'I Remember Lemuria!', the cover story of Amazing Stories for March 1945, published and promoted as substantially true by editor Ray Palmer.
propositions.assessment: This entry exists because the beat's job is to trace backwards, and the DUMB corpus is routinely dated to the 1990s when its narrative template is thirty-five years older and has a fixed, dated, commercially published origin. The artifact is a mass-market magazine with a cover date, held in library and fan collections and in the Internet Archive pulp collections; Shaver (1907-1975) and Palmer are both real, dated and documented, with a standing encyclopedia entry in the Science Fiction Encyclopedia. Crucially the truth-claim is documented too: the controversy is specifically that Shaver and Palmer asserted the material was fundamentally true while publishing it as fiction, which is the exact structural move the later corpus repeats.
propositions.proposed_band: X - VERIFICATION PENDING. Ceiling if the March 1945 issue resolves with its cover date and the Palmer editorial framing: A for a template-origin proposition, which is narrower than a claim-origin proposition and correspondingly more defensible.
supporting: Science Fiction Encyclopedia entry for Richard S. Shaver - a curated reference work with editorial standards (search snippet only)

undercutting: 'Template origin' is a weaker and vaguer proposition than 'claim origin', and it is genuinely arguable that hollow-earth literature from Symmes onward, or Bulwer-Lytton's 'The Coming Race' (1871), is the real ancestor. I did not test those and the register should not treat 1945 as a floor without doing so.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A dated commercial magazine is dispositive for when a text appeared and says nothing about influence. The discriminating question - does the later DUMB corpus DESCEND from this, or merely resemble it - is answerable by the BES 5.1.7 citation test, and there is a concrete handle for it: Thomas Allen LeVesque, the Dulce fabricator, is described in the same sources as a key figure in spreading Shaver Mystery material. If that holds, the citation test connects the 1945 template to the 1989 Dulce text through one identified person, which would be an actual documented descent rather than a resemblance.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: 'Thomas Castello', an alleged RAND-employed Dulce security technician who escaped with the 'Dulce Papers', thirty photographs and a videotape
refuted_or_hollow.origin: The persona circulates c. 1987-1991 within the Dulce cluster; Thomas Allen LeVesque, writing as 'Jason Bishop III', is reported to have admitted to author Adam Gorightly before his death in December 2018 that Castello never existed and that the material was creative writing. Christa Tilton is separately reported to have reached the same conclusion.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: The person does not resolve outside the claim. Under BES 5.4 a name that resolves to nothing in any record created for an unrelated purpose scores D0 regardless of how much text is attributed to it, and the attestation-custody rule means an anonymous account of what a named person said is one lineage with whoever is asserting - never with the person. Two caveats I insist on: the admission reaches me second-hand, after the admitter's death, through named but non-institutional channels, so the R1 route is weaker than the register's calibration presents it; and I did not run the negative search that would independently establish non-existence.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A pseudonymous authorial persona created as fiction inside a milieu already saturated by a documented AFOSI disinformation operation against Paul Bennewitz.

refuted_or_hollow.origin: Absorbed into the DIA folklore from the mid-1990s, principally via Alex Christopher's 'Pandora's Box' (1993) and 'Pandora's Box II' (1996).
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: The Denver Public Library holds a processed archival collection, 'New World Airport Commission Records', described as a public-relations body for the airport's opening, active 1994, 1997 and 1998, with correspondence to and from its president Charles Ansbacher. refuted_or_hollow.claim: 'Hangar 18' is a specific structure at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base
refuted_or_hollow.origin: A diffuse mid-century cluster rather than a single text, cemented in the nomenclature by a 1980 feature film of that title - a citogenesis route the register should trace directly.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: The Library of Congress HAER survey records Building 18 in Area B as part of the Power Plant Laboratory Complex, at the northeast corner of C and Fifth Streets - an engine and power-plant research facility, not a hangar. refuted_or_hollow.claim: The specific Denver International Airport figures - eight underground levels, a 4.5 square mile underground city, an 88.5 square mile base
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Phil Schneider, reported by Alex Christopher in 'Pandora's Box II' (1996) as Schneider's own statements.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: The figures have no source and no antecedent, and their route into circulation runs through one man's 1995 lecture circuit. The register should record the consequence: the DIA claim and the '129 DUMBs' claim are ONE lineage, not two, so any treatment of them as mutually reinforcing double-counts a single lecture. refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: The real subterranean levels beneath the terminal are the inter-concourse passenger train and the abandoned BAE automated baggage system - 26 miles of steel track, retired in 2008 and walled off, which the airport now reportedly intends to open to the public as pedestrian walkways from 2027.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: '1,477 underground bases worldwide' and '129 (or 131) secret underground bases in the United States'
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Phil Schneider's Preparedness Expo lecture, 1995 (sources differ between September and November), deposited on the Internet Archive as 'philexpo'. Schneider died in January 1996, freezing the text as canon.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: No source, no antecedent, no coordinate for any of the 129, no procurement record, no spoil accounting - and thirty years without a list. The figures function as a lineage fingerprint: any page carrying '1,477' or '129 underground bases' is in this lineage regardless of what else it says, and that test survives paraphrase and machine regeneration where shingle-matching does not. NOTE CAREFULLY: this is F, not R. The expected-record negatives here are deep and real and BES 8.4 forbids converting them into refutation - a model that refutes on negatives alone would also have refuted the Greenbrier in 1991.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A number asserted in one lecture and repeated. The genuine referent that makes it superficially plausible is the real and substantial body of documented US hardened underground facilities, which have names, records and coordinates.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: 'Report from Iron Mountain' is a genuine suppressed federal study
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Leonard C. Lewin, Dial Press, 1967, framed as leaked to him by a participant; authorship admitted by Lewin in the New York Times Book Review of 19 March 1972.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: The author confessed in print, under his own name, in a named national periodical, at a fixed date. That is BES 8's R1 branch in its cleanest possible form - an admission by the participant, documentary rather than testimonial - and it stands in instructive contrast to the Dulce R1 route, which rests on a second-hand report of a dead man's admission. The two look identical in a one-line summary and are completely different in kind. Recirculation as authentic continued through 1990s militia bootlegs and persists on live pages in 2026, including machine-generated ones.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A political satire, set at a real underground corporate records-storage facility near Hudson, New York - which is itself a different object again from the Iron Mountain / Boyers, Pennsylvania facility the register already grades at band A. Three distinct things, one word, and BES 11.1 forbids merging them on name similarity.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: A pre-Columbian 'Lizard People' city with a Key Room and gold tablets lies beneath Fort Moore Hill, Los Angeles
refuted_or_hollow.origin: G. Warren Shufelt, on readings from a self-built 'radio X-ray' device; reported by Jean Bosquet, Los Angeles Times, 29 January 1934. The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors is reported to have approved the excavation contract on 21 February 1933 with Rex McCreary, Warren Shufelt and Ray Martin on a treasure-split basis.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: It was affirmatively tested at the time, by the claimant, with the county's permission, and it failed. A shaft was sunk to roughly 250 feet at the claimed spot; no tunnels and no tablets were found; water and mud entered; funding and press attention ended and the holes were covered. A century of downtown regrading and construction has since constituted an enormous accidental search with an entirely negative result. This is not the argument from silence - it is a failed test, which is affirmative content improbable under the proposition.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A 1930s treasure-hunting venture built on an unvalidated instrument, given administrative cover by a county with nothing to lose and publicity by a metropolitan newspaper with a taste for the story.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: 'Mel's Hole', a bottomless pit on private land nine miles west of Ellensburg, Washington
refuted_or_hollow.origin: A caller identifying himself as Mel Waters on Coast to Coast AM with Art Bell, 21 February 1997, with a follow-up on 24 February 1997 and further appearances in 2000 and 2002.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Local reporters are described as having searched the Kittitas County records and found no Mel Waters as a property owner, no matching rural parcel, and no employment record for the claimed wife at Central Washington University. County deed and assessor records sit at X3 on the expected-record table - the universal CONUS floor - so this absence is maximally informative rather than routine. A thirty-person ground search of Manastash Ridge in 2002 with GPS and metal detectors, covered by the Seattle Times, found nothing. Jack Powell, then a Washington DNR geologist, stated in 2012 that such a hole is physically impossible and identified a real abandoned gold-mine shaft northwest of Ellensburg, perhaps 300 feet deep, as the plausible substrate. CAVEAT: everything above is journalists reporting that they searched the county record. The record itself is unretrieved, and it is the difference between R and F.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A performed or fabricated call, plausibly built on local knowledge of a real 300-foot abandoned mine shaft on private land.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: A national tunnel network was melted by nuclear subterrene machines, and the absence of spoil proves it
refuted_or_hollow.origin: The inference, not the documents. The documents are genuine 1970s Los Alamos research. The move from 'the AEC patented a rock-melting tunneller' to 'therefore a network was melted' traces to the 1990s fringe-book corpus, principally Richard Sauder's 'Underground Bases and Tunnels' (1995), with Schneider supplying the numbers.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: The 1972 patent's own stated advantage - that the process produces no muck or tailings - is deployed downstream to explain why the most diagnostic possible signal is missing. Spoil-volume signature sits at X3 on the expected-record table, the strongest negative available. A claim structured so that the absence of its own strongest disconfirming signal counts as support has removed its own falsifiability, and under BES 4.4 that collapses to the D0 cell at any volume of assertion. Separately: the programme record indicates transfer in 1975 and quiet termination without a full-scale prototype.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A cancelled civil-tunnelling R&D programme, funded partly by the National Science Foundation, plus the very large body of real, named, documented US deep underground construction - the Rainier Mesa U12 tunnel complex being the clearest instance, with six nuclear weapons-effects tests in U12t alone between 1970 and 1987 and a published DOE historical evaluation.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: 'Western Virginia Office of Controlled Conflict Operations' is an official designation of the Mount Weather facility
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Apparently a coinage of the Mount Weather folklore layer originating with Richard Pollock, 'The Mysterious Mountain', The Progressive, March 1976. I found no documentary attestation for it in any federal record - though I also did not search federal records for it, which is the check that would settle this.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS WITH A NAMED TEST, NOT A CONCLUSION. The phrase now appears as an alternate official name in the page titles of both the FAS Nuclear Information Project and GlobalSecurity - a T2/T3 source and a T4 source in this project's own tier table. A folklore coinage that has migrated into the nomenclature of reference sites researchers treat as institutional is the laundering pattern CAP-3 exists to catch, and here it is running through the register's own source list. The test is binary and cheap: does the phrase appear in any federal record. If it does, this finding collapses entirely and should be struck.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A journalist's characterising phrase from 1976, repeated without attribution until it acquired the appearance of nomenclature.

refuted_or_hollow.origin: The underground element is a 1990s accretion whose own origin I did NOT trace and which remains open. The documented kernel beneath it is real: Alfonso Chardy, Miami Herald, 5 July 1987, and the Brooks-North exchange in the Iran-Contra hearings of 13 July 1987.

OPEN THREADS I DID NOT CLOSE. (a) The origin of the UNDERGROUND element of the FEMA-camps claim - I traced the political kernel to 1987 and the underground accretion to nobody. (b) Whether the 1980 film 'Hangar 18' created the nomenclature it appears to describe, which would be a textbook citogenesis event. A STRUCTURAL GAP IN THE RUBRIC ITSELF, offered for consideration rather than as a finding. The expected-record framework is built for facilities where concealment is the controlling variable and silence is routine. Two entries here invert that: at Kokoweef and at Fort Moore Hill, the searchers were the PROPONENTS, funded, motivated, with lawful access, digging at the claimed location - for ninety years in one case. Their failure is signed evidence of a different and much stronger kind than a missing MILCON line, and there is no ERP profile for it. I would propose a 'proponent-searchable claim' profile where a sustained, funded, on-site negative by the claimant's own party scores as affirmative UNDERCUTS rather than as documentary absence, which would let those two entries reach R by a legitimate route instead of resting at F.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. I did not manufacture coordinates. Six of the twelve entries carry precision 'none' or 'claimed-only' and no lat/lon, because the claims themselves have never been located, and a precise pin manufactured from imprecise evidence would be the register performing its own citogenesis at the interface layer.
